effective_rules: Table 83 requires BitsPerCoordinate, BitsPerComponent, BitsPerFlag, and Decode. Type 6 legal coordinate widths are 1/2/4/8/12/16/24/32; component widths 1/2/4/8/12/16; flag width 2/4/8 with only low two bits used, valid values 0-3. Function is optional; with it each corner is one parameter t, t is interpolated throughout before Function evaluation, Decode bounds input and output components are clamped; Indexed is prohibited.

Type 6 has at least one complete patch. Each new patch gives 12 boundary controls then four corner values. Figure45/prose orders corner colors at control points x1,x4,x7,x10. Table84 flag0 is 12 points+4 colors; flags1-3 omit four shared edge points and two shared corner colors, inheriting those according to the named prior edge. Later overlapping patches shall paint over earlier patches.

Type 7 is identical to Type 6 except for ShadingType and 16 control points instead of 12. Its stream order is 12 boundary controls followed by p11,p12,p22,p21 and then the four corner colors. Table85 continuation flags reuse the corresponding edge controls and two colors; the remaining 12 controls and two colors are explicit. Function and Decode behavior inherit Type6 rules.

source_to_consumer.assessment: Source-mandated visible order is now checked through public CPU raster pixels. The initial draft sampled page-space y as raster y and saw transparency; this was a draft-oracle error, not a product failure. After correcting to raster row 74 on the 100-high page and adding literal single-red/single-blue controls, both stream orders pass in patch-order-wave102b.log.

adr_review.assessment: Nonlinear patch Function order is independently exercised by the Type6/7 parameter tests; no conflicting current behavior found.
Fold-over largest-v precedence test remains a separate within-one-patch rule and does not cover cross-patch stream ordering.
Patch geometry is passed to device tessellation; current scope does not revisit its tolerance or device-space choice.
Bounded patch color conversion lattice remains separately exercised; this audit does not claim every color-space route.
Runtime function-fault route is covered by a Type4 mesh test; patch-specific function fault behavior remains unverified, with no defect inferred.
